# Results — Study 310 (Platinum-Palladium) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The platinum/palladium ratio
(PL=F / PA=F futures price ratio) z-score mean-reversion strategy: enter the spread when
the rolling 252-day z-score exceeds ±1.5 (ratio at a ~1-year extreme), exit when z reverts
within ±0.5. Two-leg futures spread, compared against a random-direction control on
identical entry/exit dates. As-of **2026-05-31** (the partial June 2026 month is dropped).
PL=F and PA=F daily data from 2010-01-04 to 2026-05-29 via Yahoo Finance.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| PL=F (platinum front-month) | 2010-01-04 → 2026-05-29 | 4,124 | `136a4cd1f31c` |
| PA=F (palladium front-month) | 2010-01-04 → 2026-05-29 | 4,107 | `a53cb60090ad` |

PL/PA ratio range: **0.31 – 3.70**, mean **1.34** over the full period. That range is the
whole story: platinum used to trade well *above* palladium (ratio > 2), then the
2018–2022 petrol-emissions palladium boom inverted the pair (ratio fell below 0.4 —
palladium briefly cost over three times platinum), and it has since partly normalised.
The "mean" a reversion trade is supposed to anchor to was not a constant.

## Structural tests — is there a mean-reverting ratio to exploit?

| Test | Statistic | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| ADF on PL/PA ratio | p = 0.0110 | **Rejects unit root** — the ratio is statistically stationary over the full sample… |
| OU half-life (AR fit) | **475 trading days** (~22 months) | …but reversion is glacial — useless at any trading horizon |
| Engle-Granger cointegration | p = 0.7010 | **Not cointegrated** — no stable long-run link between the two prices |

> The ADF "rejects a unit root" result is a full-sample artefact: the ratio rose to 3.7,
> crashed to 0.31, and partly recovered, so over 16 years it *looks* like it returns to a
> mid-level. But the implied half-life is 475 trading days (22 months), the pair is not
> cointegrated (p = 0.70), and the round-trip was driven by a one-off demand regime
> change, not a restoring force. This is mean-reversion you cannot trade.

## Strategy results — primary: enter |z₂₅₂| > 1.5, exit |z| < 0.5

With 16 years of data and a 252-day z-score, only **26 round-trip trades** are generated.
The average holding period is **87 trading days** (~4 months).

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | skew |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Z-score reversion strategy** | 26 | **73.1%** | **−101.1** | **−0.32** | −2.23 |
| Random direction (control) | 26 | 50.0% | −117.5 | −0.41 | — |

- The HAC t-stat is **−0.32** — not merely below the |t| ≥ 2 bar, but on the *wrong side*
  of zero. The mean per-trade return is **negative**.
- The win-rate is high (73%) **and the expectancy is negative** — the textbook "many small
  wins, rare catastrophic loss" shape (skew −2.23). The catastrophic losses are the
  regime-inversion trades that bet on reversion and got run over.
- A circular block-bootstrap 95% CI on the mean is **[−705, +431] bps** — it spans zero by
  a mile. There is no edge here, in either direction, that the data can pin down.

## Cost analysis

Costs are not the executioner (the trade is infrequent), but they make a losing trade
worse, not better:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −101.1 | −0.32 |
| 5.0 bps | −106.1 | −0.34 |
| 10.0 bps | −111.1 | −0.36 |
| 20.0 bps | −121.1 | −0.39 |

## Buy-and-hold benchmark

Over 2010–2026 the two metals diverged sharply — exactly the divergence the ratio trade
mistook for a reversion opportunity:

| Asset | Total log-return | Annualised |
|---|--:|--:|
| PL=F (platinum) | +23.7% | +1.5%/yr |
| PA=F (palladium) | +117.6% | +7.4%/yr |

Palladium roughly quintupled platinum's return — a structural, not mean-reverting,
divergence.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when reversion is real

On a deterministic synthetic pair with a planted OU mean-reversion speed, the same z-score
strategy recovers a large edge over the random-direction control:

| planted OU speed | n trades | strategy HAC *t* | random HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (random walk) | 1 | n/a | n/a |
| 0.05 | 60 | +16.0 | +1.3 |
| 0.10 | 93 | +20.6 | −1.7 |
| 0.15 | 109 | +21.8 | +0.2 |
| 0.20 | 133 | +25.8 | +1.7 |

The engine is a faithful mean-reversion harvester. The real PL/PA pair simply lacks a
tradable restoring force.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** HAC *t* = −0.32 on 26 trades over 16 years, with a *negative* mean
  per-trade return (−101 bps) and a bootstrap CI [−705, +431] that swamps zero. There is
  no statistically detectable edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A 73% win-rate masks a negative expectancy driven by rare
  regime-inversion blow-ups; ~1.6 signals/year and 4-month holds. You could not have made
  money running this, gross or net.
- **Does the ratio mean-revert? — MIXED.** The full-sample ADF rejects a unit root
  (p = 0.011), so a textbook would call the ratio "stationary" — but the 475-day half-life,
  the failed cointegration (p = 0.70), and the one-off 2018–2022 demand regime change mean
  any reversion is far too slow and too structural to trade.
